sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the source to extract the following antibiotics: (a) Tetracycline (b) Streptomycin.
questions.answer: (a) Streptomyces (S. aureofaciens). (b) Streptomyces griseus.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The 'molecular scissors' in genetic engineering are ______. (b) The 'molecular glue' is ______.
questions.answer: (a) restriction endonucleases. (b) DNA ligase.

questions.q: Match: (a) Penicillin (b) Streptomycin (c) Tetracycline with (i) Penicillium (ii) Streptomyces griseus (iii) broad spectrum.
State true or false: (a) Plasmids are used as cloning vectors. (b) Biogas is produced in the presence of oxygen.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – anaerobically.

questions.q: Name the gall-producing bacterium and the plasmid used to produce transgenic plants.
questions.answer: Agrobacterium tumefaciens; Ti plasmid.

questions.q: Name two proteins and two enzymes obtained by recombinant DNA technology.
questions.answer: Proteins: insulin and growth hormone; enzymes: protease and amylase.

questions.q: Name the microorganism used for the production of (a) curd (b) alcohol.
questions.answer: (a) Lactobacillus. (b) Yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

questions.q: Name two diseases for which bioengineered vaccines have been developed.
questions.answer: Hepatitis B and rabies.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write any two advantages of biogas.
questions.answer: It is a cheap, clean fuel that saves fossil fuels, and the slurry left behind is an excellent manure.

questions.q: What are antibiotics? Differentiate broad-spectrum and narrow-spectrum antibiotics.
questions.answer: Antibiotics are chemicals produced by microbes that inhibit other microbes. Broad-spectrum (tetracycline) act on many kinds of bacteria; narrow-spectrum (penicillin) on a few.

questions.q: What is bioremediation? Give an example.
questions.answer: Cleaning of the environment using living organisms; mercury-resistant bacteria convert metallic mercury to a harmless compound.

questions.q: What is a transgenic organism? Give one example.
questions.answer: An organism carrying a foreign gene; Bt cotton or a goat producing tPA in its milk.

questions.q: What is gene therapy?
questions.answer: Replacement or correction of a defective gene by a normal gene to treat a genetic disorder.

questions.q: Write two drawbacks of antibiotics.
questions.answer: Bacteria become resistant by mutation, and antibiotics may kill useful gut bacteria or cause allergy.

questions.q: What is a clone? What is a DNA library?
questions.answer: A group of genetically identical cells or copies from one cell; a DNA library is a collection of cloned DNA fragments stored for use.

questions.q: Name the steps of the production of alcohol by yeast in brief.
questions.answer: Sterilise the fermenter, add medium and yeast, control temperature and pH, ferment sugar to alcohol and CO2, then remove the product.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Describe the steps of recombinant DNA technology.
questions.answer: Isolate the DNA, cut the gene with a restriction enzyme, cut the plasmid with the same enzyme, join with ligase to form recombinant DNA, insert into the host bacteria, grow the clone and store in a gene library.

questions.q: Explain the production of yoghurt and cheese.
questions.answer: Lactobacillus in the starter converts lactose to lactic acid; the lowered pH curdles casein, which separates from the whey; for cheese rennin is also used.

questions.q: Explain how biogas is produced.
questions.answer: Cowdung is fermented anaerobically by methanogenic bacteria in a digester at pH 6.8-7.6 producing methane and CO2; the slurry is used as manure.

questions.q: Describe the production of transgenic animals by microinjection.
questions.answer: Ova are matured and fertilised in vitro, foreign DNA is injected into the male pronucleus, the embryo develops in vitro and is implanted into a foster mother; offspring with the transgene are transgenic.

questions.q: Write the uses of biotechnology in medicine.
questions.answer: Production of insulin, growth hormone and vaccines, antibiotics, gene therapy and DNA fingerprinting.

questions.q: Describe the steps in the fermentation process for alcohol.
questions.answer: Sterilise the fermenter, select and inoculate the yeast, maintain conditions, stir and ferment, take out the product.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the tools and steps of recombinant DNA technology and its applications.
questions.answer: Restriction endonuclease, plasmids, ligase, host bacteria and cell culture; steps from cutting to cloning; applications in insulin, growth hormone, vaccines and enzymes.

questions.q: Explain transgenic plants and animals with examples.
questions.answer: Agrobacterium Ti plasmid in plants (Bt cotton), microinjection in mice and goats; uses in better crops and medicine.

questions.q: Describe antibiotics, their sources and drawbacks.
questions.answer: Definition; penicillin, streptomycin, tetracycline and their sources; broad and narrow spectrum; resistance and allergy.

questions.q: Explain gene therapy and the single-gene disorders it may treat.
questions.answer: Replacement of the defective gene with a normal gene; SCID, haemophilia, sickle-cell anaemia and phenylketonuria.
